subject: SLO & failover deep-qualify: proposed interop test plan and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Levin <sara@stratushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: SLO & failover deep-qualify: proposed interop test plan and next steps

Sara — great to meet yesterday, thanks for carving out the time for the demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the reliability tests Stratus wants to run.

Recap of what we covered:
- Redwood demo focused on multi-region failover, automatic KV cache rehydration, and per-tenant rate limiting.
- Stratus priority: predictable 99p latency under steady-state load, graceful degradation when nodes fail, and clear error budgets for production traffic.

Proposed test objectives (high level):
1) Sustained throughput: 500 qps sustained for 30m, measure 95/99/99.9 latencies and CPU/GPU utilization.
2) Failover behavior: kill a node mid-ramp, observe failover time, request retries, and tail-latency impact.
3) Region outage simulation: simulate full-region loss and validate routing to secondary region with session continuity for in-progress requests.
4) Rate-limiting & throttling: enforce per-client limits and validate error responses / retry semantics.
5) Error-budget burn scenarios: generate an injected 1% error spike and verify alerting and auto-fallback behavior.

Deliverables we propose to run during the POC:
- Interop test matrix (attached) with test definitions, SLAs, and success criteria.
- Redwood runbook for failure injection and post-test analysis.
- Shared Drive with scripts and Grafana dashboards.

Ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm the core acceptance criteria (particularly the 99p latency target and acceptable failover window)?
- Please propose 2x 2-hour slots next week for an initial ramp and one full failover test.
- Who on your side should we loop in for deep ops coordination? (cc: suggested ops contacts would help).

Attaching interop-test-matrix.xlsx for reference. Ben (cc) will follow up with the concrete test scripts and a West/East schedule.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sara Levin <sara@stratushealth.com>

Cc: eng-ops@stratushealth.com, rajiv@stratushealth.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO & failover deep-qualify: proposed interop test plan and next steps

Marcus — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock schedules: 

1) Latency targets: Our production SLA needs 99p <= 150ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) and 99p <= 450ms for longer completions. Is Redwood able to provide historical 99p telemetry for a comparable workload?
2) Error budgets: we currently allow 0.5% p95 error budget per week. We need to understand how Redwood surfaces error attribution (model vs infra) in the logs.
3) Failover tolerance: primary ask is session continuity — we may have in-flight requests that should either complete or be retried transparently. Can Redwood demonstrate request-level continuity or only per-session rehydration?
4) Rate limits: we expect per-API-key concurrent request caps + soft throttling window. How configurable is that?

On timing: we can do a morning window (10:00–12:00 PT) on Tue 4/13 or Thu 4/15. Ops will join if we confirm Tuesday.

Also — standard procurement asks: SOC 2 report (or link), IP/data residency confirmation, and a brief summary of any default rate limits and token billing quirks.

I can share an internal ops contact if useful: Claire Wu (eng-ops@stratushealth.com) who will run the tests on our side.

Best,
Sara Levin
Director of Product, Stratus Health
sara@stratushealth.com

Attachments: none

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLO & failover deep-qualify: proposed interop test plan and next steps

Folks — putting together a concrete technical plan to answer Sara's questions and run the tests. High-level notes and what I'll deliver by EOD Monday: 

Planned test harness and metrics:
- Traffic generator: open-source k6 + our tokenized client (script: k6/redwood_qps_test.js) to reproduce the workload shapes (short/long prompts).
- Telemetry: Grafana dashboards (qps, p95/p99/p999, GPU utilization, queue lengths) + request traces with trace IDs forwarded to Stratus.
- Attribution: spans include "inference-kernel" and "runtime-queue" so we can point to model vs infra. We'll provide an attribution worksheet after each run.

Config specifics (defaults vs configurable):
- Default per-key: 200 concurrent connections, burst to 400 for 30s. All limits configurable per-deal; we can set Stratus to 1k concurrent for POC.
- Retry semantics: idempotent GETs auto-retry x2 with exponential backoff; generation calls return structured 429 with retry-after and we support client-side retry guidance.
- Failover: we support request proxying to a warm standby region; for session continuity we do best-effort rehydration — in-flight requests may be retried if the client re-sends with the same trace id. We'll run an explicit test to validate how many requests succeed vs how many need client retry.

Test cases we'll provide (scripts and acceptance):
- Ramp-to-steady: ramp 0→500 qps in 10m, sustain 30m, acceptance: 99p latency under target and error rate <0.5%.
- Node-kill during steady: kill a worker GPU node, acceptance: failover completes within 60s and p99 spike returns to baseline within 5 minutes.
- Region cutover: announce BGP-like outage to simulate region loss, acceptance: secondary region serves traffic within 90s and stateless requests remain successful; for stateful sessions we measure how many requests required client retry.
- Rate-limit boundary: increase concurrent clients to trigger soft throttling, acceptance: system returns standardized 429 and backoff guidance; no silent drops.

Attachments and artifacts I'll drop in the Drive: test scripts, runbook (redwood-runbook.md), dashboards, and a short HowTo for Claire.

I'll also attach a sanitized SOC2 excerpt and the telemetry retention policy. Marcus — can you confirm the two-hour window Sara suggested works and I'll book infra and the on-call SRE?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-runbook.md (text, 18KB); telemetry-sample.png (image, 240KB)

Thanks, Sara — appreciate the quick clarifications. Confirming we can meet the proposed acceptance criteria and outlining the next concrete steps so your ops team can sign off: 

Confirmed items:
- Latency: we'll target 99p <= 150ms (<=256 tokens) and 99p <= 450ms (long completions) as the POC acceptance thresholds.
- Error budget: we'll measure and report weekly error rates; for the POC we'll aim for <0.5% total error rate and provide per-span attribution.
- Rate-limits: we'll set a POC profile at 1k concurrent connections per key with a configurable soft window (we'll provide a policy doc).
- Failover: we'll run both node-level and region-level failover tests. We will instrument request trace IDs and provide a CSV with request outcome (succeeded, retried, failed) so you can validate session continuity.

Proposed schedule (please confirm one):
- Option A (preferred): Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–12:00 PT — ramp test + node-kill validation
- Option B: Thu 2027-04-15 10:00–12:00 PT — same scope if Tue not available

Responsibilities & owners:
- Redwood: run traffic generator, kill node(s) per the plan, share dashboards and attribution worksheet (Owner: Ben Carter).
- Stratus: provide on-call ops and validate acceptance criteria (Owner: Claire Wu).
- Contract/procurement: Marcus to share SOC2 excerpt and draft MSA addendum for POC; Priya to assist on any deal-configured rate limit terms.

Acceptance criteria checklist (quick):
- Test completed during agreed window
- 99p latency within targets for both prompt lengths
- Error rate < 0.5%
- Failover time within agreed windows and documented retry outcomes
- Delivery of dashboards + attribution CSV within 24h of test

Action items (who/when):
- Ben: drop scripts and runbook in Drive and confirm infra reservation (EOD Mon).
- Marcus: send SOC2 excerpt and the one-page POC addendum (today).
- Claire / Stratus: confirm Option A or B and provide the final test attendee list (today).

Once you confirm Option A we'll send a calendar invite with the runbook and pre-test checklist. Looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Regards,
